    AI Overview
    The Rooney Rule is an NFL policy established in 2003 requiring teams to interview minority candidates for head coaching, senior football operation, and executive positions to promote diverse leadership
    . Named after former Steelers owner Dan Rooney, it aims to ensure equal opportunity, though it has faced criticism for resulting in "sham" interviews and mixed success in increasing minority hiring. 
    How the Rooney Rule Works & Requirements 
    • Mandatory Interviews: Teams must interview at least two minority candidates for head coaching vacancies and at least one minority candidate for senior operational roles (e.g., General Manager) and offensive assistant positions.
    • Expansion:
      The rule has expanded over time to include women and a broader range of positions, including quarterback coaches.
    • Expansion: In 2022, it was expanded to require at least one ethnic minority or woman on the offensive coaching staff.
    • Consequences: Failure to comply with the policy can result in significant fines from the league. 
    Purpose and Benefits 
    • Diversity Goal: To break down systemic barriers and increase the number of minorities in leadership roles within the NFL.
    • Increased Opportunities: It forces decision-makers to expand their networks and consider candidates who might otherwise be overlooked, potentially mitigating unconscious bias. 
    Criticisms and Challenges 
    • "Sham" Interviews: Critics, including coaches like Brian Flores, argue that teams often interview minority candidates only to fulfill the requirement rather than to seriously consider them for the position.
    • Effectiveness: Despite the rule, the number of Black head coaches has not consistently remained high, leading to criticism that it does not go far enough to ensure true equity.
    • Legal Challenges: As of 2026, the rule is facing legal threats, with claims that it constitutes illegal race-based discrimination. 
    Impact on Other Industries
    The rule has inspired similar, voluntary diversity initiatives in corporate hiring beyond the sports industry.
